chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Ibrahim ibn Ishaq al-Talaqani (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id, the servant of Bani Hashim, narrated to us. He said: Al-Mundhir ibn Muhammad narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn Isma'il al-Maythami narrated to us. He said: Isma'il ibn al-Fadl narrated to us. He said: I asked Aba Abdillah Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq (peace be upon him)

about Allah, the Blessed and Exalted — will He be seen in the Resurrection? So he said: Glorified be Allah and exalted is He greatly above that! O Ibn al-Fadl! Surely, the sights only perceive that which has a colour and a modality, and Allah is the Creator of colours and modalities.

key_terms.المعاد: The Resurrection / Return — the Day of Judgment when all are raised, central to Islamic eschatology
key_terms.خالق الألوان والكيفية: Creator of colours and modalities — God cannot be an instance of what He creates
key_terms.لون وكيفية: Colour and modality — the physical attributes that make an object perceptible to eyesight; Imam al-Sadiq argues God transcends these categories

ai.seo_question: Can God be seen on the Day of Resurrection according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Isma'il ibn al-Fadl asks Imam al-Sadiq (as) the fundamental theological question of whether God will be seen on the Day of Resurrection (a question debated between various Islamic schools of thought). The Imam responds with an emphatic glorification formula — 'subhan Allah' — expressing that God is far above such a notion. He then provides a rational argument: sight can only perceive objects that have color and physical form (kayfiyya), and since God is the Creator of colors and modalities, He transcends the category of things that can be perceived by sight.
